name: Can a load-bearing wall be removed to expand a kitchen?

mainEntity.name: Can a load-bearing wall be removed to expand a kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can remove a load-bearing wall to expand your kitchen, but it requires installing an engineered support beam and temporary shoring. During an open-concept conversion or kitchen expansion, removing a structural wall transfers upper-floor or roof loads onto a steel or engineered wood beam supported by new posts and footings. A licensed general contractor coordinates structural engineering assessments to verify load paths before cutting into framing, ensuring ceiling stability and proper transfer of structural weight down to the foundation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, load-bearing walls can be removed if an engineered support beam and posts are installed to safely carry the overhead weight.
